issues.description: The primary moderator (moral disapproval) is measured using a single Likert-type item for each behavior. Single-item measures often suffer from low reliability and cannot capture the multi-dimensional nature of moral constructs (e.g., social stigma vs. personal values).
issues.quote: For each substance, we will ask participants to rate their agreement with the following statement “I believe that using ________ is morally wrong” on a scale of 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree).

issues.description: The author plans to standardize and then average items from the NIDA-ASSIST. However, the items use different response scales (0-5 for frequency vs. 0, 3, 6 for concern/control). Standardizing items with different variances and then averaging them can lead to biased composites where items with higher original variance are under-weighted.
issues.quote: Responses to each of the above five items will be standardized, and an average will be taken for each substance of interest.

issues.description: The study uses cross-sectional data to test if moral incongruence 'predicts' or 'influences' addiction. However, the relationship could be reversed: individuals who feel they have lost control over a behavior (addiction) may develop moral disapproval of that behavior as a form of self-stigma or cognitive dissonance reduction.
issues.quote: the present work seeks to clarify if moral incongruence (the interaction of behavioral frequency and moral disapproval of a behavior) is uniquely related to sexual behavior, or if it generalizes to other addictions as well.

issues.description: The plan to redefine the Smallest Effect Size of Interest (SESOI) if the primary hypothesis is disconfirmed is a form of 'p-hacking' or analytic flexibility that undermines the purpose of a Registered Report. Success criteria should be fixed a priori.
issues.quote: In the event that, contrary to hypotheses, the effects of moral incongruence for gambling and substances exceed our region of equivalence based on our SESOI, we will conduct exploratory analyses wherein we redefine the region of equivalence using the lower bounds of the 95% CI for the standardized estimate for our pornography outcome.

issues.description: The oversample of 1,500 sports bettors (37.5% of the total sample) may significantly bias the results for the gambling domain. Sports bettors often have different demographic and moral profiles compared to general gamblers (e.g., lottery players or slot machine users), limiting the generalizability of the 'gambling' findings.
issues.quote: we will also recruit an additional 1,500 adults with recent (past year) history of wagering on sports generally or sporting events specifically.

issues.description: The measures use inconsistent timeframes: BPS (6 months), PGSI (12 months), and NIDA-ASSIST (3 months). This makes direct comparisons of 'moral incongruence' across different behaviors statistically and conceptually problematic.
issues.quote: In the last 6 months, have any of these situations happened to you... [BPS] vs. Thinking about the last 12 months… [PGSI] vs. In the past three months, how often... [ASSIST]

issues.description: The Brief Pornography Screen (BPS) includes an item about feeling 'guilty.' Since moral disapproval is the moderator, the dependent variable is partially composed of the moderator's conceptual domain, leading to inflated correlations (criterion contamination).
issues.quote: 5. You continue to use pornography even though you feel guilty about it.

issues.description: The power analysis shows that for prescription drug misuse (n=140) and illicit substances (n=240), the study is severely underpowered to detect the interaction effect (power = .301 and .472 respectively). Moderation effects typically require much larger samples than main effects.
issues.quote: it is possible, if not probable, that our final sample sizes will fall below the minimum size required to detect effects that small (See Table 2).

issues.description: The definition of pornography provided to participants is restricted to 'genital area.' This may exclude many forms of sexually explicit media that users consider 'pornography' and which trigger moral incongruence, leading to an underestimation of use frequency.
issues.quote: pornography refers to any sexually explicit films, video clips or pictures displaying the genital area

issues.description: The manuscript relies on 'proprietary data collection standards' for quality control. For a Registered Report, specific attention checks, speeder thresholds, and data cleaning rules must be explicitly stated to ensure replicability.
issues.quote: As this data will be obtained via YouGov Opinion Polling, certain measures of quality control and responsiveness are guaranteed as a part of their data collection process based on their proprietary data collection standards.

issues.description: The authors plan to conduct 10 separate moderation analyses. While they mention Holm-adjustment for bivariate correlations, they do not specify a correction for the primary hypothesis tests, increasing the Type I error rate.
issues.quote: In total, we will conduct 10 moderation analyses for moral disapproval and frequency

issues.description: The text states that gambling frequency will be an 'average across gambling behaviors,' but the supplemental materials show a single-item measure for 'Gambled or placed bets at all.'
issues.quote: To form a measure of gambling frequency, an average across gambling behaviors will be taken.

issues.description: Grouping all 'Illegal/Illicit Drugs' into a single moral disapproval item is problematic. A participant may view cannabis as morally acceptable but heroin as morally wrong; a single item for the whole category creates measurement noise.
issues.quote: I believe that using illegal/illicit drugs is morally wrong.

issues.description: The study claims to address the 'full spectrum of addictions,' but relies solely on a U.S. sample. Morality and its relationship to behavior are deeply cultural; findings may not generalize to secular European or highly religious non-Western contexts.
issues.quote: the target sample size will be 2,500 American adults that match nationally representative norms

issues.description: The author suggests using Diagonally Weighted Least Squares (DWLS) in lavaan if OLS assumptions are violated. DWLS is intended for ordinal data in SEM, but the primary analysis is a moderation with a continuous interaction term. Using DWLS for a simple moderation model without specifying the latent structure is unconventional.
issues.quote: we will construct latent variable models using the lavaan package... using diagonally weighted least squares estimation

issues.description: The model controls for age, gender, and religiousness, but ignores personality traits like Neuroticism or Conscientiousness, which are known to correlate with both moral scrupulosity and self-reported addiction symptoms.
issues.quote: In each case, we intend on including religiousness, age, and gender as covariates

issues.description: The inclusion criteria require 'past year' use, but the NIDA-ASSIST items for problematic use (the DV) only ask about the 'past three months.' This will exclude participants who used the substance 4-12 months ago but still have relevant moral views or history of addiction.
issues.quote: key measures will be restricted to those who have engaged in the behavior within the past year... [but ASSIST items ask] In the past three months, how often...

issues.description: The moral disapproval items do not distinguish between 'use' and 'abuse.' A participant might believe alcohol use is morally acceptable but alcohol *addiction* is morally wrong, which would confound the interaction effect.
issues.quote: I believe that drinking alcohol is morally wrong.

issues.description: The author plans to take the 'average of standardized responses' for religiousness. Standardizing Likert items before averaging is unnecessary if they share a scale and can make the resulting index harder to interpret.
issues.quote: Religiousness will be measured via the average of standardized responses to three items

issues.description: The manuscript mentions using an 'Interactive Shiny application' for visualization and testing interactions but does not provide the version or the specific R code/package that powers the 'Interactive' app, which is necessary for computational reproducibility.
issues.quote: we will make use of the Interactive Shiny application (McCabe et al., 2018).
